items.briefing:
South Australia has launched a Royal Commission into artificial intelligence, reflecting growing government scrutiny of AI risks and ethics across the country. Separately, privacy advocates are urging Australia to ban smart glasses capable of covert filming, raising concerns about surveillance in public spaces — including workplaces and training environments. An Australian startup, Quantum Lock, is also making headlines for developing new technology to detect cyberattacks on embedded devices using quantum physics.

As AI adoption grows — with Australian cloud AI spending tipped to reach AUD $1.5 billion — staff should be mindful of what they share in AI tools and be cautious around unfamiliar wearable devices in your workplace.

**Tip:** Avoid entering personal or organisational information into AI tools unless your organisation has approved them for that purpose.

featured.title: South Australia launches Royal Commission into artificial intelligence
featured.quote: South Australia's Royal Commission into AI signals government-level scrutiny of AI risks for Australian businesses.
